items.text:
Thomas Straker’s namesake London hit makes its stateside debut in NYC this weekend. | Thomas Streat/Straker’s

This is Eater’s guide to all the new restaurants, bars, and cafes that have opened this week in October 2026 Throughout the month, we’ll update the list weekly (see: September, August, July, June, May, April, March, February, January). When we’ve been to a place, we will then include a few openings on our heatmaps (Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, cocktail bars) to let you know the ones we like. If there’s an opening in your neighborhood that we’ve missed, let us know at ny@eater.com.

October 7

Spotlight

Soho: London chef and internet butter evangelist Thomas Straker takes over the former Lucky Strike, Keith McNally’s now-closed Soho fixture, for his first restaurant outside the U.K. A late-September opening date for Straker’s was pushed back to Saturday, October 10. The New York restaurant centers on an open kitchen surrounded by steel and green stone, leather banquettes, dark wood, and warm lighting. Expect the modern British cooking style with Italian leanings that defines the Notting Hill original that opened in 2022. 59 Grand Street, at West Broadway

And the rest…

Brooklyn Heights: Brooklyn’s charming new Georgian restaurant Bebo, open since late September, pays homage to grandmas everywhere with comfort foods like khachapuri, vibrant dips, and crockets of soup in a cozy space surrounded by fringed lampshades, cottage curtains, and antique plateware. 145 Atlantic Avenue, between Henry and Clinton streets, Brooklyn

Bronx: After 14 years, neighborhood sports bar Triona’s closed its original location after the Chicago Bears game on Monday, September 28, but reopened next door on Friday, October 2, as Triona’s Vintage Sporting Club. The landmarked Scheffel Hall building dating back to the late-1800s was a German beer hall and restaurant and later housed the German-American Athletic Club and Fat Tuesday’s jazz club. Vintage sports memorabilia joins more than 20 screens and an updated Irish-leaning pub menu, with a continued love for the Bears and Michigan Wolverines. 190 Third Avenue, at East 17th Street

Chelsea: A chic taste of Verona landed in New York on Thursday, October 1, with the arrival of Italian wine bar and bistro Bar Lento. Lento, the Italian word for “slow,” features a brick-framed backdrop with a secret garden inside. The warm setup showcases a wine list of whites, bubbles, and pét-nats from Sardinia to Veneto to go along with seasonal plates like bruschetta and fluke ceviche in a citrus tomato vinaigrette. 158 Eighth Avenue, near West18th Street

Chinatown: Something Smells Fishy, a casual Japanese seafood counter that accepts walk-ins only, specializes in customizable kaisendon rice bowls topped with the likes of raw tuna, salmon, fluke, and uni. 95A Elizabeth Street, near Grand Street

Crown Heights: Brooklyn Surf & Soul, a new takeout spot serving seafood and soul food, opened on October 3. It’ll offer shrimp po’ boy sandwiches, whiting sandwiches, shrimp and grits, seafood boils, fried chicken, and more. 602 Nostrand Avenue, near Pacific Street

East Village: Table Mercato, Boston’s cult-favorite Italian sandwich shop that specializes in crispy chicken cutlets shoved between freshly baked focaccia, added its first NYC location in late September. Chef Jen Royle’s popular Sicilian and spicy vodka Parm sandwiches, priced in the mid-$20s a pop, commanded immediate long lines out front (open 11 a.m. until sell-out). There are also house-made chips, onion dip, and rainbow cookies. 214 E. 10th Street, between First and Second avenues

Financial District: Nationwide ramen bar Kyuramen debuted a trio of fast-casual spots on one 9-to-5 strip in NY on Thursday, October 1. Kyuramen Express slings ramen, udon, rice bowls, sushi, onigiri, and appetizers; Bao Dumpling is a Chinese takeout with a knack for dumplings; and Aokō Matcha offers specialty green drinks and desserts. Open daily from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. for dine-in, takeout, and delivery. 40 Gold Street, near Fulton Street

Lincoln Center: Prolific French chef Daniel Boulud returns across from NYC’s cultural hub in a big way on Thursday, October 8, with the opening of Brasserie Boulud — a consolidation of his closed Upper West Side restaurants (Bar Boulud, Boulud Sud, and Épicerie Boulud) into one massive, 10,000-square-foot flagship. The classically French-leaning Brasserie Boulud features the greatest hits from each dearly missed restaurant in one combined menu. Expect seafood towers, French onion soup, steak frites, lobster souffle, and boudin blanc, along with the return of Boulud’s cult-favorite DB Burger. 1900 Broadway, at Lincoln Plaza

Lower East Side: Australia’s popular and prolific Gelato Messina has made its American debut, with the opening of Softville on October 1. Continuing the city’s fancy soft serve moment, Softville will offer it, made using dairy from Ronnybrook Farm in the Hudson Valley, alongside an extensive and rotating menu of sauces and toppings. It also offers loaded sundaes, such as a birthday cake sundae featuring fior di latte soft serve, butter cake, strawberry pudding, “birthday crumble,” strawberry and white chocolate sauce, cream cheese chantilly cream, and sprinkles. A collaboration with Studio Jeremyville, the shop is described as an “art-led concept store,” in which Studio Jeremyville sculptures and other art will be on display. The art studio has worked with Messina since its early days, creating murals for its stores. 137 Orchard Street, between Rivington and Delancey streets

Lower East Side: Brazilian restaurant Iara opened on Friday, October 2, from chef Vitor Mendes, who previously worked at Brooklyn hot spot Theodora. Mendes cites a trip to his home country of Brazil following his father’s death as inspiration for the restaurant. Before it, he told Eater NY, “I thought that my own culture was rice, beans, and barbecue, as a lot of people might think.” At Iara, he’ll employ cassava in many ways: in the crispy cubes of tapioca served with yellowfin tuna and smoked biquinho peppers, in the vinaigrette paired with his hiramasi ceviche, in the fries that accompany his picanha, and more. 205 Allen Street, at East Houston Street

Park Slope: After shuttering his 120-year-old family bakery in Carroll Gardens earlier this spring, James Caputo is back in the baking business with Caputo Bagels, which opened Monday, October 5. The new bagel shop, a collaboration with Miriam owner Rafi Hasid next door, is all about hand-rolled sourdough bagels, open-face and breakfast sandwiches, as well a familiar take on the bake shop’s famed lard bread. 81 Fifth Avenue, near Prospect Place, Brooklyn

Red Hook: All-day diner and bar Vals debuted in Brooklyn at the beginning of October with a menu full of waffles, Denver omelets, blue-plate specials like spaghetti and meatballs, funnel cakes, and milkshakes. Located in the revived Fort Defiance, Vals’ name nods to the nearby Valentino Pier. Nicely priced drinks at the newly expanded bar include draft cocktails, well drinks, beer-shot combos, Negronis, martinis, and more. The new hangout comes from Victoria Viscusi, chef Allie Gassaway, and Laine Pelka, the latter two of which previously worked in the same space before. 347 Van Brunt Street, at Wolcott Street, Brooklyn

Theater District: Diner 24, the Gramercy greasy spoon known for its giant shakes, hot dogs, and burgers served by singing waiters, added a flagship corner location in the heart of Times Square on Wednesday, October 6. Located right under the historical Lambs clubhouse, the new 235-seat Diner 24 that’s open around the clock also hosts hourly performances from actors with Broadway backgrounds from a dedicated 20-foot stage upstairs. “Mamma Mia” and milkshakes, anyone? 1674 Broadway, at 52nd Street

Times Square: Southern food chain Kitchen + Kocktails by Kevin Kelley, which started in Dallas in 2020, opened its first location in New York City. The restaurant, which is the chain’s largest, will serve dishes such as Cajun crab cakes, fried seafood and chicken, smothered steak, jerk lamb chops, and shrimp and grits. The opening continues the restaurant’s national expansion. It also has locations in Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, Miami, Philadelphia, and Washington, D.C., and will soon be opening in Boston and New Orleans. 7 Times Square, at 7th Avenue and 41st Street

West Village: Camari Mick’s long-awaited Calabash, billed as an Afro-Caribbean bakery and brasserie, opened for daytime service on Friday, October 2. Running from Thursday to Sunday, daytime service will feature Mick’s acclaimed baked goods, including sticky buns, coconut canelés, and beef patty croissants, plus cornbread pancakes with salted maple sabayon. Dinner service begins on October 9 and will be available for a single 6:30 p.m. seating on Friday and Saturday nights via prepaid bookings. It will offer dishes including suya steak frites using plantain fries and asun pasta with goat ragu and pappardelle. There’s no alcohol here, but there are fermented drinks and NA cocktails. 183 Christopher Street, near Weehawken Street

West Village: The team behind Zimmi’s expands next door on Wednesday, October 7, with the debut of a tiny 15-seat wine bar and cafe called Bar à Part. Look for small plates, an extensive wine list, as well as savory and sweet pastries from acclaimed pastry chef Clodagh Manning – the Ireland native who previously worked at London’s now-closed Lyle’s. 72 Bedford Street, at Commerce Street

Williamsburg: A new steakhouse landed in the neighborhood with the opening of Booth’s Extra Fine on October 6. The restaurant comes from the team behind Nobody Told Me; it gets its name from chef Nick Pfannersteil’s grandfather, Booth, a Milwaukee car salesman with a penchant for steak and martinis. The menu will feature the requisite steaks and martinis, plus horseradish burgers, truffle ravioli, pork chops, rum cherry sundaes, and more. A nightly Martini Hour from 4 to 6 p.m. will offer $12 martinis, $5 mini hot dogs, $2 oysters, and half-priced caviar. The location previously housed Mighty Quinn’s BBQ. 62 South 2nd Street, near Wythe Avenue

Upper East Side: Prolific Southern chicken chain Zaxbys made its Manhattan debut on Wednesday, September 30. Along with its breaded chicken “fingerz” and a dozen sauces, the menu includes Buffalo wings and a salad section it calls “zalads.” Atlanta-based Zaxbys, founded in 1990, has more than 1,000 locations across 24 states. Its only other NYC storefront sits in the Bronx. 1267 First Avenue, between 68th and 69th streets

Upper East Side: NoMad cocktail lounge Obvio – home to the New York Times’ “Martini of the Year” – starts a semi-permanent residency at its Upper East Side sibling Casa Cruz on Thursday, October 1. Every Thursday to Saturday night, the second floor of the Beaux-Arts mansion – redesigned with Obvio’s giraffe-patterned calling card – imports Obvio favorites like the Tamarind Mezcalito along with pisco-centric drink debuts like a Marmalade Martini from beverage director Amy Racine. Chef John Fraser’s popular tartare tacos and burger join new caviar cones stuffed with Toro tuna. 36 E. 61st Street, between Park and Madison avenues

items.text:
Welcome to the Eater Cocktail Heatmap, focusing on the hottest new bar openings in New York every month.

Eater editors do thorough reporting on the most exciting restaurant openings to hit the city, as well as smaller openings worth having on the radar. In this monthly map, we narrow the field to cocktail bars that are drawing the most excitement, buzz, crowds, and early positive chatter, focusing on spots that have only been open for six months or less. When an Eater editor has already been to a place, we share insider tips on what to expect and what’s worth ordering as well.

New to the list in October: We’ve added Japanese cocktail bar Don’t Be Shy in Hudson Square; massive Chinese-leaning cocktail bar/restaurant/karaoke lounge Rewind in Long Island City; South Asian speakeasy Jam & Jaggery in the East Village; and retro bars FKA in the East Village and Velvet Cowboy on the Upper West Side. For now, we’ve removed Bar Chimera, Peek Inn, and Hidden Rivers Beer Garden.

For related drinking guides, check out Eater NY’s picks for the best cocktail bars, dive bars, and wine bars. And for more New York dining recommendations, check out the new hotspots in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens. In need of an insider’s perspective on how to eat well, no matter where you are in NYC? Pick up our book: The Eater Guide to New York City.

The Jacob’s Pickles team turned its space on the Upper West Side (which relocated to Columbus Avenue) into Velvet Cowboy, a new 1970s Southwestern cocktail bar, in September. Find $5 bar snacks, like a take on the McRib sandwich, chili-cheese fries, and a huge funnel cake hanging from a stand.

A massive new restaurant-cocktail bar-karaoke lounge, Rewind, opened in Long Island City this September and is co-founded with AYS Hospitality, which runs Mr. Moto’s restaurant portfolio. The drinks menu, developed by beverage director Ken Chen, who had been at Taipei gastropub Indulge Experimental Bistro, took cues from tea, the Chinese zodiac, and the five elements. Tipsy Blossom represents fire signs and bitter elements, made with whisky, shochu, chrysanthemum, pear, hawthorn, licorice root, and goji berry. The food menu includes truffle-mushroom congee, Taiwanese fried chicken, and wagyu donburi. Per the name, people enter the space by pressing a “rewind” button on a retro boombox outside.

The team behind West Village cocktail lounge Dandelion expanded with Keepers, a new neighborhood-leaning bar and pizzeria, in July. Drinks, courtesy of Ricky Dolinsky (formerly of the View), include interesting Negronis such as the Black Forest, a drinkable homage to Ben & Jerry’s Cherry Garcia; spritzes; and frozens. Food-wise, find crispy tavern pies.

Bernie and Herb’s comes from a trio of 169 Bar alums who wanted to do a neighborhood spot that’s affordable and stays open until late. The bar opened in July, housed in the space that had been part of Coffee Shop, the Brazilian late-night icon in the area for 30 years. Look for drinks around $10 and inexpensive bar food like hot dogs, pulled pork sandwiches, and more.

FKA, which stands for “Formerly Known As,” is all about retro vibes since it opened in September in the East Village. Look for dollar East Coast oysters; dishes like lamb tartare, pimento cheese, Frito pies, and cheeseburgers; activities like pinball and Big Buck Hunter; and drinks like strawberry daiquiris, natural wines, and $8 beer-and-shot combos.

Chef Aarthi Sampath debuted a new speakeasy underneath her East Village restaurant Drāvida in September. Jam & Jaggery takes on the same South Asian foundation, with drinks like the Dirty Currytini with olive vermouth and curry leaves, and the Gola Chaat with shochu, yogurt, pomegranate, tamarind, herbs, and aloo bhujia, the latter of which is a spiced boiled potato snack. Sampath is offering some of her upstairs snacks, along with an Indian-ish burger.

The team, whose bar history includes Bar Valentina and Employees Only, took over the former Bandits space with a French-leaning bar. Bar Etienne opened in the West Village in August, with a very banana-y rum cocktail along with tomato martinis, chocolate Negronis, and wines. The bistro food menu includes steak au poivre and French onion-grilled cheeses, plus desserts created in collaboration with nearby Claude Bakery, such as tarte tatin and that chocolate cake.

New Hudson Square cocktail bar Don’t Be Shy is meant to evoke Tokyo’s stylish Ginza district since it opened in September. Head bartender Shinya Yamao, who worked at now-closed Piora and Tribeca sake bar Shigure, developed a Japanese cocktail menu with a special Trip to Japan menu available only at the nine-seat bar counter, exploring Japanese history and regionality, like the Edo, made with a potato-miso-flavored vodka and a sweet potato-Campari ice cube. items.title: Fugu Film: Documentary “Gun Fish” Explores Secrets of a Risky Food Culture
items.summary: Many kinds of Japanese seafood are celebrated around the world, but fugu—the blowfish species famous for the deadly toxin they retain when not prepared
items.text:
Many kinds of Japanese seafood are celebrated around the world, but fugu—the blowfish species famous for the deadly toxin they retain when not prepared correctly—may be among the most famous. A new documentary sheds light on the “gun fish,” named for its lethal power, and the culinary culture that has appeared around it.

A Perilous Delicacy

(© Gun Fish Film Partners)

The documentary Gun Fish opens at an official Tokyo facility dedicated to removing poison from fugu. At the time of filming in 2017, it was found in Tsukiji, before the world-famous wholesale seafood market moved to Toyosu. As you might assume from the name, this was a place where fugu, the general Japanese term for all varieties of blowfish, headed to market had their poisonous organs removed. In the off season lasting from spring through summer, it was also an exam venue for Tokyo’s fugu cook license.

Handling fugu is strictly controlled by rules set at the prefectural level. There is no national standard for acquiring or labeling the various licenses, but basically all are designed to ensure that cooks have the necessary knowledge and skills to serve fugu safely to the public.

The exam for obtaining a fugu cook license requires detailed knowledge of various fugu varieties. (© Gun Fish Film Partners)

Getting certified requires being able to identify different fugu species, differentiate the edible and inedible parts of each, and safely clean the fish. Fugu poison, a form of tetrodotoxin, is mostly concentrated in the liver and ovaries, but the poisonous parts can vary by species. Of the 70 species of fugu that live in the seas around Japan, 22 have edible flesh, while 18 have edible milt (testes), and only 11 have edible skin and fins. The road to becoming a pro fugu cook requires a vast amount of knowledge and experience.

While filming at the toxin-removal station, documentary director Uno Wataru’s great discovery was the chef-in-training Nameki Yukari, who became his film’s main focus. Just 23 years old at the time of filming, she first takes the screen near the very beginning of her studies, at which point she seems not to have absorbed any of her lessons.

Uno looks back on her progress. “As we were filming her training, my first thought was that we wouldn’t be able to use any of the footage. But two weeks later, it was like watching a totally different person handling the fugu. It was fascinating. I called up a friend who’d been helping with the filming and said, ‘We’ve got our main character. We’re on our way to a movie.’ I remember being really excited.”

Nameki Yukari identifying fugu species. (© Gun Fish Film Partners)

The Future of Fugu Fishing

The first half of the film shows scenes of Nameki’s intense training, interwoven with easy-to-understand explorations of fugu biology, culture, and history that sketch out this fish’s unusual position.

One bit of trivia mentioned is how Shimonoseki in Yamaguchi Prefecture became the national center for all things fugu. It stands near many fertile fishing grounds and fugu had long been a part of local cuisine, but the decisive moment came when it was the first place in Japan for the official ban on serving fugu to be lifted. That was the work of Japan’s first prime minister, Yamaguchi-born Itō Hirobumi (1841–1909), who greatly enjoyed a fugu meal in Shimonoseki. The restaurant where he ate it, named Shunpanrō, is also where the peace treaty ending the First Sino-Japanese War (1894–95) was signed. The lifting of that ban allowed for fugu restaurants to flourish in Shimonoseki and encouraged rapid development in fugu dressing and cooking skills.

Haedomari, Shimonoseki’s fugu-specialty market, opened in 1974. Fugu caught all over Japan are brought here and the poisonous parts removed before the fish are shipped out for further processing nationwide. Shimonoseki thus rose to prominence not as a fishing center for fugu, but a major logistics hub for the fugu industry.

The traditional “bag auction” at Haedomari Market. The buyers indicated their bids silently, using finger signals inside the bag. (© Gun Fish Film Partners)

Today, though, the once-uncontested strength of the “Shimonoseki brand” is on the wane. “Even as farmed fish now accounts for 90 percent of the market, the wild-caught fugu fishing grounds have been migrating further and further north, with many now caught in Tokyo Bay, Sotobō in Chiba, or the seas off Sōma in Fukushima,” explains Uno. “The shift away from shipping fugu all the way down to Shimonoseki has only accelerated in the nine years since we filmed. I think Shimonoseki itself is standing at a crossroads.”

Osaka’s Original Fugu

When speaking of fugu, Osaka stands alongside Shimonoseki as a must-mention. It is the largest consumer market in Japan, accounting for 60% of all the fugu eaten on its own. Many buyers bring it in directly from the fishing ports, making it cheaper for consumers. As a result, its reputation as a high-end fish is relatively unknown in the city. Osaka also has a lot of licensed fugu cooks, and over the years has adopted its own unique approach to licensing. Uno got officially registered as a fugu cook in Osaka in 2017, and saw for himself the difference from Tokyo.

Director Uno Wataru. (© Nippon.com)

“For example, in Tokyo, there is a fixed pass rate, and if you don’t hit the required line, they’re just like, ‘See you next year.’ But in Osaka, they train you until you have the knowledge you need. Rather than detailed prep skills, the focus is on being able to remove the poisonous parts. You’re expected to learn all the cooking skills that come after that in the kitchen. It’s a fitting philosophy for Osaka, which has so many fugu restaurants.”

Kushida Kōichi, the fugu expert behind Kushida Suisan at Tsukiji (now Toyosu) market. (© Gun Fish Film Partners)

At the same time, the Zenkoku Fugu Renmei (National Fugu Federation), which features prominently in the film, is promoting uniform licensing across Japan, since the lack of a single standard makes it difficult to get import restrictions lifted in the EU and other global markets. Their efforts resulted in the Ministry of Health, Labor, and Welfare releasing guidelines on eliminating variance in prefectural rules. Tokyo responded by easing the qualifications for taking the exam and the knowledge tested, while Osaka has moved from a training-based system to an exam-based one.

Shimonoseki’s annual Fuku (a local variation on the fugu name) Memorial Festival, which brings fugu professionals together from all over Japan. (© Gun Fish Film Partners)

The Meat of Fugu Cuisine

After viewers are given a crash-course in basic fugu knowledge in the first half, Gun Fish presents a heated debate around a core question in fugu food culture: What if fugu was made nonpoisonous?

The starting point is the taboo of eating the liver. The toxicity of fugu liver has long been common knowledge, but on hearing that it is also incredibly delicious, many people have apparently given in to temptation and lost their lives. One of them was famed kabuki actor Bandō Mitsugorō VIII (1906–75). The living national treasure’s 1975 death by fugu poisoning resulted in a law strictly punishing the sale of fugu organs.

A traditional Ishikawa Prefecture dish of pickled fugu ovaries, which are just as dangerous as the liver. The only way to make them edible is this traditional method of fermenting them for over three years in brine and rice bran. (© Gun Fish Film Partners)

But in 2004, a Nagasaki University research team investigating fugu poison succeeded in making farm-raised fugu poison-free, leading to an article in the English-language science magazine Nature. If fugu liver became safe to eat, it would surely mark a watershed moment in Japanese food culture.

Saga Prefecture sought to leverage this breakthrough in a local revitalization scheme. It applied to the MHLW for special certification as a Fugu Liver Zone, where people would be allowed to sell and eat nonpoisonous farmed fugu liver. Predictably, the National Fugu Federation and the city of Shimonoseki opposed the effort, saying a single accident could destroy trust in the nation’s fugu cuisine as a whole. The scheme has been rejected three times by the ministry and abandoned entirely.

The documentary takes up this liver-eating debate, introducing both the pro and anti sides as it explores the current state of fugu cuisine in Japan.

”I think if fugu weren’t poisonous, we wouldn’t have a movie. I see a certain Japanese-ness expressed in the opposing values that the debate brings to light. I wanted to show both sides equal respect, so I labeled them the ‘adventurers’ and the ‘custodians.’ Neither side is good nor bad; each is taking the stance of following through on their claims and their beliefs. And I find that really cool.”

Kamei Kazuhiro (right), owner chef of Kyoto restaurant Fugu Ryōri Tomoe, demonstrates the technique of slicing fugu sashimi. (© Gun Fish Film Partners)

Betting Their Lives on Fugu

The film introduces people working with fugu in all sorts of roles, each one sharing their own love of the fish. Their positions are all different, but they share the same ideals of broadening the dishes using this unique fish, preserving the culture of its cuisine, and nurturing it for the future.

Says the director: ”When I was editing the film, I grew convinced that bringing all of these people together into one film was something only I could do. That is one of the biggest things I learned through all this.”

Kitahama Kiichi, owner of Osaka’s Kitahachi restaurant and founder of the Fugu Museum, is one of the world’s leading fugu researchers. He insists that “Fugu brings people together.” (© Gun Fish Film Partners)

In all, a decade passed from the start of filming until the documentary’s completion, spanning the COVID-19 pandemic.

Uno laughs: “Before I started looking into it, I had the same image of fugu as most, that it’s this poisonous, high-class fish. I never imagined I’d get so into it! This must be the true danger of fugu!”

items.text:
A股大盘再度回落至年内低位，但国投证券首席策略分析师林荣雄认为，转机或已临近。


在10月11日最新发布的策略周报中，林荣雄团队提出，10月下旬美股AI龙头三季报及资本开支指引的集中披露，叠加国内A股三季报窗口与DeepSeek筹备科创板上市，将构成AI产业景气的重要验证期。若届时长端美债利率随财政预期降温而回落，A股科技板块年内第二波行情有望明确开启。


该团队将当前市场定性为从"第三象限向第四象限过渡"的关键节点——即在国内K型经济分化尚未收敛、但美债利率压制有望边际缓和的组合下，AI科技有望凭借独立景气度率先获得估值修复。林荣雄强调，"在国内宏观经济K型分化没有收敛之前，资本市场'无科技不成牛'，最终结束'M非A'信仰要坚定。"


报告同时指出，经过前期风格调整，国证价值与国证成长的指数比值已回到年初附近，成长板块此前积累的风险已有明显消化，当前配置赔率正在改善，四季度可适度向成长倾斜。

大盘回落至敏感点位，市场等待两大转机信号

林荣雄团队指出，当前A股大方向的定价由国内盈利扩散（K型分化）与海外流动性（美债利率）双因子共同决定。市场真正需要的答案只有两个：一是看到国内K型经济收敛，内需提振出台真招实招，扭转收入信心不足的预期；二是看到海外长端美债利率能够边际缓和，至少不再继续创新高，令市场在定价层面逐渐对高利率脱敏。

目前两个条件均未完全满足。国内方面，9月制造业PMI回升至52左右、重回扩张区间，地产贴息政策与稳楼市组合拳相继落地，央行三季度货币政策例会亦强调继续实施适度宽松货币政策。但该团队认为，这些举措更多是通过四季度适当加码政策使全年经济增速满足年初预设目标下限，对居民资产负债表收缩与房价预期的扭转仍需时间，K型经济分化的收敛目前看依然无法确认。


海外方面，美国9月非农新增就业仅2.9万人，远低于预期的8.9万人，10月加息概率已明确下降。但若价格压力再次上升，12月加息仍可能成为政策选项。市场一致认为美债利率易涨难跌，高位状态短期内难以改变，更多需要等待市场对高利率呈现出脱敏状态。

AI中美分化背后：定价逻辑转变而非产业趋势逆转

8月以来，美股费城半导体指数上涨约11.15%，而A股AI硬件板块却先涨后跌，光模块、半导体等方向本周领跌，中美科技资产阶段性收益背离明显。

林荣雄团队将这一背离归结为四方面原因：其一，在资金流动层面，高美债利率下全球AI资产定价收圈至美股AI科技核心龙头；其二，在产业趋势层面，9月下旬美国参议员再度提出针对中国光模块的法案，A股海外算力链开始额外计入供应商政策风险，即便近期订单尚未受到明显影响，但限制扩大、客户增加替代供应商的担忧已形成估值折价；其三，前期大幅上涨后的高估值需要时间消化，目前国证价值与国证成长的指数比值已回到年初附近，成长此前积累风险已有明显消化；其四，美股开始出现"AI硬切软"迹象，市场从"AI=买芯片"进入"AI全栈重估"阶段，数据云、数据库、企业软件等此前预期较低的环节，一旦证明真实增量收入，估值弹性反而更大。

在此认知基础上，林荣雄团队对年内AI科技行情后续作出两阶段预判，并提示所有展望均建立在一定假设条件之上。

第二阶段为11月至12月，团队提示存在估值切换与地缘政治引发的波动风险。进入12月，AWS re:Invent、甲骨文及博通财报将继续提供产业需求验证线索，Gemini 4扩大开放、Mistral新模型开放权重等进展亦可能带来新的预期变化。

该团队同时设定了三个核心前提：全球宏观不出现"黑天鹅"（如美联储激进加息周期与美伊冲突明显加剧）；AI科技后续盈利增长斜率超过贴现率上行幅度；经过一个季度情绪消化与交易拥挤回落至中位水平。"只要产业逻辑没问题，四季度AI科技行情回归概率在增大，这才是年内胜负手。"

四象限框架：当前处于杠铃策略阶段，等待向科技主导切换

林荣雄团队以"国内K型分化—海外美债利率"四象限框架作为配置决策的核心工具。在当前K型分化不收敛、美债利率高位的组合下，对应的市场结构为"杠铃策略"：资金倾向两端配置，一端是有产业景气支撑的科技龙头，另一端是红利、资源、高股息等现金流资产，中间大量普通行业缺少明确方向。

报告数据显示，当前价值与成长风格的相对比值已来到近一年最高水平，科技、成长、微盘、红利和大盘在经历一轮分化和收敛后，年内收益率已回到同一起点附近。


该团队判断，一旦美债利率出现边际回落信号，市场有望从"K型分化不收敛+美债利率下行"象限进一步切换，对应少数高景气科技资产反复创新高、出现面向年内二顶反弹的"科技M顶"结构。

财政发力叠加产业政策，为科技成长提供阶段性支撑

国内政策面亦出现边际积极变化。10月9日，财政部宣布安排使用地方政府债务结存限额5500亿元，规模较去年增加500亿元，为近年来最大。其中专项债务结存限额2500亿元重点支持"六张网"建设，涵盖新型电网、算力网、新一代通信网等数字基础设施领域。


与前两年不同，本次安排未明确列示化债清欠用途，资金投向更突出县区财力保障和有效投资。同日，中共中央、国务院印发《关于发展新质生产力的意见》，内容覆盖技术研发、成果转化、产业升级、融资制度和人才机制，共提出五个方面、19项重点举措。


林荣雄团队认为，上述财政加力与产业政策联动，短期可能强化科技成长板块的政策预期，其中数字基础设施、电网等方向可能带来结构性投资需求；更持续的受益，仍应寻找能把技术转化为订单、收入和效率改善的企业。

高盛在最新资产配置报告中同时上调股票和债券评级，其对平衡型投资组合前景的判断出现重要转变。


据追风交易台消息，高盛将全球股票评级上调至3个月维度超配，与12个月维度保持一致，理由是近期估值回调改善了进入三季度财报季的赔率。与此同时，高盛将债券评级上调至12个月维度超配，认为随着通胀正常化和央行政策立场趋于温和，长久期债券的中期配置价值正在上升。


信用债方面，高盛将3个月评级下调至低配，与12个月立场保持一致，认为当前利差水平相对全收益率仍处低位，风险回报不及股票。


高盛在报告中指出，其宏观基准情景依然偏向乐观：经济增长保持健康、衰退风险低企，通胀动能有望在2027年前持续消退。这一"金发女孩"式组合将为平衡型投资组合提供更有利的环境，债券也有望逐步从拖累因子转变为有效对冲工具。

风险资产承压，利率与能源价格成核心扰动

自夏季以来，全球风险资产整体处于整固状态，利率上行和能源价格压力日益侵蚀盈利增长带来的顺风效应。全球股市尽管底层盈利表现稳健，但在上行利率环境下整体横盘，估值遭到明显压缩。


压力最为集中的领域包括对利率敏感的小市值股、房地产及基础设施板块。高盛报告显示，MSCI全球指数12个月远期市盈率年内已累计下滑近20%，属于晚周期中罕见的大幅去评级。与此同时，利率上行开始向信用市场蔓延，企业信用利差显著扩大，欧元区主权风险溢价也出现重新定价。


高盛风险偏好指标（RAI）在过去两周内从此前高位骤降至零，其货币政策分项（RAI PC2）已跌至2000年以来的最低水平之一——上一次录得类似读数是在2022年。高盛指出，RAI PC2的急剧下滑在历史上通常会改善股票和债券的回报赔率，因为这往往预示着利率压力趋近极限并为后续缓解创造条件。

重新看多股票：盈利韧性支撑，估值回调创造机会

高盛将3个月股票评级重新上调至超配，核心逻辑在于盈利增长依然稳健而估值已充分回调。高盛美股策略团队预计2027年标普500盈利增速达18%（剔除股权重估相关"其他收入"的基效影响），并预期三季度财报季将在美国和欧洲均呈现超预期表现。


高盛指出，若利率出现缓解，叠加AI应用落地加速带动实质性收入和盈利改善，股票存在估值扩张空间。在区域配置上，高盛维持亚洲和美国超配、欧洲低配，并建议采用"哑铃"策略：一端配置AI受益的科技股，另一端精选对利率敏感、具备高股息和低波动特征的防御性股票，后者有望受益于未来利率回落。


高盛同时提示，近期主要下行风险来自利率和能源价格的进一步上行，以及美国中期选举不确定性可能推高权益波动率。

中长期转向超配债券：从拖累到对冲

尽管在3个月维度维持债券中性评级，高盛已将12个月维度债券评级上调至超配，视之为资产配置立场的重要战略性转变。


高盛认为，当前收益率水平已赋予长久期债券更好的非对称性：利率下行带来的潜在收益已超过利率进一步上行可能造成的损失。支撑这一判断的核心逻辑包括：通胀预期改善、更高的票息收益及再投资收益率，以及央行政策立场趋于温和。


高盛经济学家预计美联储、欧洲央行和英国央行均仅剩一次加息空间，并有望于明年开始降息，而市场当前定价已反映美联储超过三次、欧洲央行至少两次、英国央行近四次的加息预期——与高盛基准情景存在显著落差。这一背景进一步强化了债券配置的中期价值。


在区域选择上，高盛维持对美国、英国和德国10年期国债的超配，低配日本。高盛指出，法国OAT利差走阔引发了对美债和德债的相对安全需求，为上述市场提供了额外支撑。

低配信用债：利差对冲价值不足

高盛将信用债3个月评级下调至低配，与12个月立场一致，并明确表示在股票与信用债之间倾向于选择股票。


报告指出，信用利差在近期风险规避环境中已落后于股票表现，延续了年内的相对弱势。即便经过近期利差扩张，信用利差相对全收益率的占比仍处历史低位——以美国投资级企业指数为例，信用利差仅占全收益率的15%，而近年平均值约为45%。


高盛信用策略团队维持美元信用优于欧元信用的观点，倾向于高收益债券而非杠杆贷款，同时低配欧元区AT1相对高收益债。此外，持续的债券供给压力和企业加杠杆趋势构成额外阻力。

"金发女孩"宏观情景，平衡型组合受益

高盛认为，名义增长动能正趋近峰值，但主要驱动力是通胀正常化而非实际增长放缓。这一组合——经济增长保持健康而通胀持续消退——与"金发女孩"情景高度吻合，历史经验表明这是60/40平衡型投资组合表现最佳的宏观环境。


高盛动态资产配置模型显示，在其宏观基准情景下，未来12个月60/40组合的回撤风险已降至历史区间低端，右尾风险（12个月涨幅超过20%）的概率接近历史无条件均值。


高盛同时指出，其模型尚未充分纳入AI资本开支热潮对盈利的推升效应，因此可能低估股票的上行潜力——这与1990年代末的情况类似，当时模型同样未能捕捉到后期科技股的超额涨幅。

战术对冲：期权保护仍具吸引力

高盛建议在超配股票的同时保留战术性现金仓位，并通过期权工具选择性增加股票敞口。目前全资产类别隐含波动率整体处于低位，VIX维持在15附近，而利率波动率（MOVE指数）相对股票波动率已升至2024年以来最高水平，两者背离值得关注。


具体对冲工具方面，高盛推荐以下三类策略：其一，VIX看涨期权价差，可应对宏观冲击触发相关性骤升的情景，当前最大赔付比率处于历史高位；其二，短端利率接受方期权（front-end receiver swaptions），在衰退情景下可提供优于标普500虚值看跌期权的收益，当前短端远期利率的大幅上行也创造了更具吸引力的入场点；其三，针对欧元区财政风险，欧元兑美元和欧元兑瑞郎的看跌期权提供定向对冲，但需主权压力进一步扩散方能兑现收益。

items.text:
最近两个月来，美国股市波动较大，也波及其他地区。美国股市波动既有其货币政策变化的影响，也有市场对AI板块资本开支持续性的担忧，而前者又加剧了后者。简而言之，今年美国AI领域的几家大公司资本开支快速上升，明年虽然增速可能比今年慢，但仍然较快。但另一方面，AI企业的收入却面临较大不确定性，经营现金流已经与资本开支相若，一些公司开始通过发债支持资本开支。而美国国债收益率上升更加剧了市场的疑虑：在收入面临不确定性的情况下，资本开支如何维持，这是市场普遍关心的话题。

图表1：美国AI企业资本开支与经营现金流相若


注：图中数据为微软、亚马逊、谷歌、Meta、甲骨文之和
资料来源：Epoch AI，Bloomberg，iFinD，中金公司研究部

AI是个新兴产业，其技术突破时点以及商业收入增速天然难以预测。我们将不聚焦收入，而选择从资金配置的视角出发，探讨美国AI资本开支的潜在资金来源。实际上，投资是收入的来源，如果资本开支难以保障，那收入增长也就缺乏支持。换言之，资本开支与收入并非互相割裂的两个变量。因此，讨论资本开支的融资状况也有助于我们判断收入的前景。


我们首先从AI产业的属性出发，分析该产业在吸引资金方面的优势。第二部分我们分析自1990年代以来美国社会资金供应的变化。具体而言，我们剖析美国的“金融化”如何重塑其流动性。“金融化”并无统一定义，其体现也比较复杂，但我们认为至少有两点对分析AI融资有意义。从宏观视角来看，金融化意味着广义流动性与GDP之比上升，通俗地说，就是社会上的“钱”逐步增多。从微观来说，金融化意味着新的金融产品数量与种类增加。金融产品（比如衍生品）使得资金“活”起来，也提升资产的流动性。当然，宏观层面与微观层面并非割裂，金融产品数量增加本身也可能导致宏观层面的流动性增加。


剑桥大学国王学院院长、Financial Times资深记者Gillian Tett 在《欢迎来到金融棉花糖时代》里面通俗地阐述了美国金融化现象，并回顾了金融“棉花糖”这个词的来源。因此，我们不妨借用金融“棉花糖”这个形象的说法来近似代指美国金融化。[1]


虽然美国在2008年次贷危机之后加强了金融监管，尤其是对银行的监管，但总体而言，其金融化现象并未明显逆转。在此基础上，我们回顾了1990年以来美国两次泡沫破裂前的金融化：1990年代的科网金融化与次贷危机之前的房地产金融化。我们然后分析当前美国AI产业的金融化所处的阶段，最后也分析当前美国AI板块可能面临的流动性风险。


AI：既有科技属性，也有“类地产”属性

我们认为，AI既有科技属性，也有“类地产”属性（固定资产占比较高），意味着既可以通过股权融资，也可以通过债权融资（抵押贷款）。


AI的科技属性无需赘述，其技术进步和生产效率提升似乎较科网企业更快。其中一个体现是，AI对劳动力的依赖较科网企业低，甚至可以替代劳动力。从中观数据来看，自2022年ChatGPT发布以来，美国通信和计算机行业的非农就业小幅缩减了6%。与此不同，从1995年8月美国网景公司上市（美国科网泡沫元年）到2000年3月美国科网泡沫破裂之间，其通信和计算机行业的非农就业则上升了60%多。

图表2：科网革命时期与AI年代美国通信、计算机行业就业走势分化

金融化提升流动性

金融化并没有统一定义。我们不妨引用Epstein（2005）的定义：金融目的、金融市场、金融主体以及金融机构，在国内与国际经济运行当中发挥愈发重要的作用[2]。这个定义隐含的意思是金融在资源配置中的作用上升。


不同学派认为金融化的驱动因素不一样[3]。新马克思主义认为，70年代后资本主义实体投资回报率下滑，过剩资本涌入金融投机是资本主义金融化的主因。后凯恩斯主义认为，企业治理转向股东价值优先，导致企业缩减实体投资、加大股票回购与金融资产配置，结果是金融投资挤出实体资本积累。而新古典主义则认为金融自由化、资产证券化提升资产流动性，优化资源配置，是经济发展的进步。尽管不同理论学派对金融化的发展理解不同，罗煜（2017）认为，布雷顿森林体系瓦解、全球进入纯信用货币制度，无疑为金融化创造了条件。具体而言，他认为支付媒介方面，实物现金占比大幅减少，交易变为账户数字划转，交易成本下降，交易规模增加。价值贮藏方面，各类金融资产起到了“准货币”的价值储藏功能，广义货币边界更加广阔。[4]


金融化的主要体现有以下几个方面[5]：（1）广义流动性更加充裕。比如广义流动性与GDP之比提升，金融部门的利润占比上升，金融部门规模增长相对更快。（2）低流动资产变成高流动资产。各类新型金融工具层出不穷，证券化将非流动资产转化为流动资产，金融交易规模大幅增长。（3）资本利润的获取愈发依靠金融渠道，而非实体贸易与商品生产。例如，企业利润更加依赖投资收益。（4）资本市场型金融体系话语权持续扩张。例如，股市/GDP、债务/GDP比值不断上涨，银行信贷/GDP比值下降。（5）企业治理中更加重视股东价值。例如，美股市场上回购增加。


从宏观方面来看，1990年代中期后，美国广义流动性与GDP之比趋势上升，较M2与GDP之比大约高20个百分点。金融危机后，美国加强了金融监管，美国银行部门的贷款业务相对放缓，但美国银行资产/GDP之比未见收缩，银行部门非贷款业务继续扩张。

美国科网与地产金融化的经验

美国在自1980年代以来有两次加速金融化的经验，一个是1990年代的科网金融化，另一个是2000年后的地产金融化。1990年代科网金融化表现为美国VC大幅增长和股权融资热，增加了资金使用方式，使得资金能够流动起来。这个阶段金融化的一个重要驱动因素是对养老金投资约束放松，促进VC发展，IPO提供退出渠道，释放VC资金，吸引更多资金进入。而2000年代美国地产金融化，既创造新流动性，也增加流动性使用方式，其主要体现是通过证券化，使得房地产贷款机构释放资本金，突破资产负债表约束，形成更多的贷款，创造了新的流动性。而证券化进一步让更多金融机构参与到地产金融化，资金使用方式增多。


美国企业的股权融资方式包括私人股权融资和公开股权融资。在初创期主要是通过私人股权融资，在成长期之后，通过公开股权融资方式。1979年后，美国放松对养老金的投资限制，促进了VC的大幅增长。VC把“没有抵押品的互联网创业公司”变成比较容易融资的企业，IPO提供退出渠道，将股权占用的资金释放出来，再形成新的投资。IPO退出也帮助VC吸引更多资金。


具体而言，1979年之前，《雇员退休收入保障法》（Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974）的“审慎人规则（Prudent‑Man Rule）”限制美国养老金参与初创企业投资。1979 年美国劳工部对“审慎人规则”做出澄清，养老金做投资判断要看整个组合的风险分散效果，不再要求每个项目都必须风险低。改革后养老金可以增加配置风险投资，机构LP大规模入场，深刻改变美国VC行业资金来源结构，美国VC新增规模和投资额呈现大幅增长。从美国VC资金来源看，在1978年只有约15%来自养老金，而到了1990年，约有53%来自养老金。美国VC的募资额和投资额也是在1990年代开始出现快速增长。

为了实现更好的退出，1990年代末期，美国IPO大幅折价发行，特别是科技股，以吸引更多投资者参与。新成立、历史业绩少的VC，有很强动机推动被投企业 IPO，接受较高IPO折价，利用IPO首日暴涨制造成功退出案例，向LP展示业绩，方便募集下一期VC基金。1990年代后期IPO退出回报非常可观，进一步刺激LP向 VC大规模出资。而随着IPO发行量的增加，上市企业的平均质量下降。VC支持的上市科技企业平均年龄从9年（1991年）下降到4年（1999年）。


2000年后美国地产金融化既通过衍生品盘活了存量资产，也带动广义货币的扩张，与债权融资紧密相关。各类金融机构通过资产证券化，将房地产资产转化成可交易、可抵押、可加杠杆的金融资产，从而把房地产市场和资本市场、银行体系及影子银行体系连接起来。住房按揭MBS证券化的首要作用是盘活存量信贷资产，让原有货币更加活跃，提高货币流通速度；同时银行回笼资金后可以持续向家庭发放新增贷款，通过商业银行信贷派生机制，带来广义货币扩张。


盘活存量资产的方式包括信用增强、再次证券化、给抵押贷款加“保险”等，使得原本难以“流动”的资产变成“可流动”的资产。信用增强（Credit enhancement）大约有三个方式：（1）信用分层（Tranching），将抵押贷款转换成了不同风险等级的证券，满足不同的投资者的需求；（2）超额抵押（Over‑collateralization）：资产池的规模大于对外发行全部证券的本金总和，多出的那一部分资产就是超额抵押，用来吸纳亏损；（3）超额利差（Excess spread）：抵押贷款利率高于MBS的利率，保证利差为正。


CDO（Collateralized Debt Obligation）将以次级贷款为底层资产的MBS再次进行证券化、分层，转换成不同等级的证券。此外，CDS（Credit Default Swap）给抵押贷款加上一层“保险”，进一步提升其流动性。


数据显示，1980年代以后，美国贷款/GDP比例大幅上升，其中居民地产贷款上升最多。1995年，居民抵押贷款与GDP之比不足50%，而2007年该比例超过80%。从2001年到2006年，美国抵押贷款证券化比例大幅上升，特别是Alt-A和Sub-prime这些质量较差的抵押贷款证券化比例上升较快。例如，Alt-A级抵押贷款的证券化比例从19%（2001年）上升到了91%（2006年），Sub-prime级抵押贷款的证券化比例从46%（2001年）上升到了75%（2006年）。


美国抵押贷款持有人从银行转向非银。早期美国住宅证券化主要由Fannie Mae、Freddie Mac、Ginnie Mae等政府支持机构参与，后期越来越多的非政府支持机构开始参与抵押贷款证券化（包括投资银行）。通过证券化方式，政府支持机构（如房地美、房利美）、ABS发行人持有占比2006年超过60%。

短期风险

前面的分析意味着，在美国金融化的大背景下，加上AI公司既有比科网公司更强的科技属性，又有“类地产”属性，AI公司既可以通过股权融资，也可以通过债权融资。而与历史上的科网革命和房地产相比，美国AI公司当前金融化尚处于早期阶段，其资金来源无需过度担忧。但这不是说，我们就可以忽视短期的流动性波动风险，尤其是油价居高不下、美国加息路径不清晰的情况下。


回顾历史，当年美国科网泡沫与地产泡沫破灭前同时出现三个现象：（1）高杠杆。科网革命时期，美国大量Dotcom公司上市，Shiller PE ratio从17倍（1990年）上涨到44倍（2000年）。次贷危机前，美国家庭部门宏观杠杆率从70%（2000年）上升到98%（2007年）；（2）基本面走弱。2000年左右，美国互联网用户渗透率出现拐点，而2006年开始，美国房贷违约率开始上升；（3）融资条件系统性收紧。美联储从1998年开始加息，联邦基金利率从4.75%（1998年）上升至6.5%（2000年）。次贷危机前，联邦基金利率从1.0%（2003年）上升到5.23%（2006年）。


当前，对于AI公司来说，这三个现象特征都还不显著。目前美国企业部门杠杆率相对还较低，股市估值也不算非常高；美国经济基本还比较强劲，名义增长在5%左右，以Mag 7为代表的大科技公司营收、利润增速还较高；融资条件暂时还未见明显持续的收紧。


但是，短期风险仍需要关注，可能对AI企业融资产生扰动。目前美国融资需求旺盛，而随着通胀上升，资金面边际紧张。近期，实际融资压力（实际利率TIPs）走高，市场对AI产业链高杠杆的持续性产生顾虑。


2026年9月，英格兰央行金融政策委员会指出AI债务上升，以及其不够透明，对风险评估带来困难，而随着金融条件收紧，信贷市场（包括私募信贷）相对比较脆弱[11]。2026年5月，美联储在《金融稳定报告》中指出，AI以及私募信贷是近期需要关注的风险[12]。美联储认为随着资本支出越来越多地依赖债务融资，增加了系统的杠杆效应；私人信贷面临着越来越大的压力，包括投资者的赎回、情绪恶化，以及人工智能带来的信贷质量影响。2026年9月，标普将Oracle的评级下调至BBB-，仅高于垃圾级[13]。自美联储在2026年9月加息后，到9月底，Coreweave一些高收益债的收益率上涨了超过0.5个百分点[14]。2026年7月，Meta新发120亿美元债券，为数据中心进行融资，债券收益率为7.5%，融资成本要比2025年10月发行270亿美元债券时高出0.4个百分点[15]。

具体来看，短期需关注两类风险。一是融资条件收紧，削弱私人投资动能。若美联储加息，或银行收紧贷款标准，企业融资成本和资金获取难度可能上升，进而拖累私人投资扩张。二是短期融资压力加剧，放大流动性风险。回购与资产支持商业票据市场利差仍高于常态，提示部分市场主体的短期融资压力尚未消退。若此时货币政策进一步收紧，可能增加债务续借难度，并放大短期资金市场的波动。

AI是个新兴产业，其技术突破时点以及商业收入增速天然难以预测。我们将不聚焦收入，而选择从资金配置的视角出发，探讨美国AI资本开支的潜在资金来源。实际上，投资是收入的来源，如果资本开支难以保障，那收入增长也就缺乏支持。换言之，资本开支与收入并非互相割裂的两个变量。因此，讨论资本开支的融资状况也有助于我们判断收入的前景。

我们首先从AI产业的属性出发，分析该产业在吸引资金方面的优势。第二部分我们分析自1990年代以来美国社会资金供应的变化。具体而言，我们剖析美国的“金融化”如何重塑其流动性。“金融化”并无统一定义，其体现也比较复杂，但我们认为至少有两点对分析AI融资有意义。从宏观视角来看，金融化意味着广义流动性与GDP之比上升，通俗地说，就是社会上的“钱”逐步增多。从微观来说，金融化意味着新的金融产品数量与种类增加。金融产品（比如衍生品）使得资金“活”起来，也提升资产的流动性。当然，宏观层面与微观层面并非割裂，金融产品数量增加本身也可能导致宏观层面的流动性增加。
剑桥大学国王学院院长、Financial Times资深记者Gillian Tett 在《欢迎来到金融棉花糖时代》里面通俗地阐述了美国金融化现象，并回顾了金融“棉花糖”这个词的来源。因此，我们不妨借用金融“棉花糖”这个形象的说法来近似代指美国金融化。[1]
虽然美国在2008年次贷危机之后加强了金融监管，尤其是对银行的监管，但总体而言，其金融化现象并未明显逆转。在此基础上，我们回顾了1990年以来美国两次泡沫破裂前的金融化：1990年代的科网金融化与次贷危机之前的房地产金融化。我们然后分析当前美国AI产业的金融化所处的阶段，最后也分析当前美国AI板块可能面临的流动性风险。
AI：既有科技属性，也有“类地产”属性
我们认为，AI既有科技属性，也有“类地产”属性（固定资产占比较高），意味着既可以通过股权融资，也可以通过债权融资（抵押贷款）。
AI的科技属性无需赘述，其技术进步和生产效率提升似乎较科网企业更快。其中一个体现是，AI对劳动力的依赖较科网企业低，甚至可以替代劳动力。从中观数据来看，自2022年ChatGPT发布以来，美国通信和计算机行业的非农就业小幅缩减了6%。与此不同，从1995年8月美国网景公司上市（美国科网泡沫元年）到2000年3月美国科网泡沫破裂之间，其通信和计算机行业的非农就业则上升了60%多。

金融化提升流动性
金融化并没有统一定义。我们不妨引用Epstein（2005）的定义：金融目的、金融市场、金融主体以及金融机构，在国内与国际经济运行当中发挥愈发重要的作用[2]。这个定义隐含的意思是金融在资源配置中的作用上升。

不同学派认为金融化的驱动因素不一样[3]。新马克思主义认为，70年代后资本主义实体投资回报率下滑，过剩资本涌入金融投机是资本主义金融化的主因。后凯恩斯主义认为，企业治理转向股东价值优先，导致企业缩减实体投资、加大股票回购与金融资产配置，结果是金融投资挤出实体资本积累。而新古典主义则认为金融自由化、资产证券化提升资产流动性，优化资源配置，是经济发展的进步。尽管不同理论学派对金融化的发展理解不同，罗煜（2017）认为，布雷顿森林体系瓦解、全球进入纯信用货币制度，无疑为金融化创造了条件。具体而言，他认为支付媒介方面，实物现金占比大幅减少，交易变为账户数字划转，交易成本下降，交易规模增加。价值贮藏方面，各类金融资产起到了“准货币”的价值储藏功能，广义货币边界更加广阔。[4]

金融化的主要体现有以下几个方面[5]：（1）广义流动性更加充裕。比如广义流动性与GDP之比提升，金融部门的利润占比上升，金融部门规模增长相对更快。（2）低流动资产变成高流动资产。各类新型金融工具层出不穷，证券化将非流动资产转化为流动资产，金融交易规模大幅增长。（3）资本利润的获取愈发依靠金融渠道，而非实体贸易与商品生产。例如，企业利润更加依赖投资收益。（4）资本市场型金融体系话语权持续扩张。例如，股市/GDP、债务/GDP比值不断上涨，银行信贷/GDP比值下降。（5）企业治理中更加重视股东价值。例如，美股市场上回购增加。
从宏观方面来看，1990年代中期后，美国广义流动性与GDP之比趋势上升，较M2与GDP之比大约高20个百分点。金融危机后，美国加强了金融监管，美国银行部门的贷款业务相对放缓，但美国银行资产/GDP之比未见收缩，银行部门非贷款业务继续扩张。

美国科网与地产金融化的经验

美国在自1980年代以来有两次加速金融化的经验，一个是1990年代的科网金融化，另一个是2000年后的地产金融化。1990年代科网金融化表现为美国VC大幅增长和股权融资热，增加了资金使用方式，使得资金能够流动起来。这个阶段金融化的一个重要驱动因素是对养老金投资约束放松，促进VC发展，IPO提供退出渠道，释放VC资金，吸引更多资金进入。而2000年代美国地产金融化，既创造新流动性，也增加流动性使用方式，其主要体现是通过证券化，使得房地产贷款机构释放资本金，突破资产负债表约束，形成更多的贷款，创造了新的流动性。而证券化进一步让更多金融机构参与到地产金融化，资金使用方式增多。
美国企业的股权融资方式包括私人股权融资和公开股权融资。在初创期主要是通过私人股权融资，在成长期之后，通过公开股权融资方式。1979年后，美国放松对养老金的投资限制，促进了VC的大幅增长。VC把“没有抵押品的互联网创业公司”变成比较容易融资的企业，IPO提供退出渠道，将股权占用的资金释放出来，再形成新的投资。IPO退出也帮助VC吸引更多资金。

具体而言，1979年之前，《雇员退休收入保障法》（Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974）的“审慎人规则（Prudent‑Man Rule）”限制美国养老金参与初创企业投资。1979 年美国劳工部对“审慎人规则”做出澄清，养老金做投资判断要看整个组合的风险分散效果，不再要求每个项目都必须风险低。改革后养老金可以增加配置风险投资，机构LP大规模入场，深刻改变美国VC行业资金来源结构，美国VC新增规模和投资额呈现大幅增长。从美国VC资金来源看，在1978年只有约15%来自养老金，而到了1990年，约有53%来自养老金。美国VC的募资额和投资额也是在1990年代开始出现快速增长。

为了实现更好的退出，1990年代末期，美国IPO大幅折价发行，特别是科技股，以吸引更多投资者参与。新成立、历史业绩少的VC，有很强动机推动被投企业 IPO，接受较高IPO折价，利用IPO首日暴涨制造成功退出案例，向LP展示业绩，方便募集下一期VC基金。1990年代后期IPO退出回报非常可观，进一步刺激LP向 VC大规模出资。而随着IPO发行量的增加，上市企业的平均质量下降。VC支持的上市科技企业平均年龄从9年（1991年）下降到4年（1999年）。

2000年后美国地产金融化既通过衍生品盘活了存量资产，也带动广义货币的扩张，与债权融资紧密相关。各类金融机构通过资产证券化，将房地产资产转化成可交易、可抵押、可加杠杆的金融资产，从而把房地产市场和资本市场、银行体系及影子银行体系连接起来。住房按揭MBS证券化的首要作用是盘活存量信贷资产，让原有货币更加活跃，提高货币流通速度；同时银行回笼资金后可以持续向家庭发放新增贷款，通过商业银行信贷派生机制，带来广义货币扩张。

盘活存量资产的方式包括信用增强、再次证券化、给抵押贷款加“保险”等，使得原本难以“流动”的资产变成“可流动”的资产。信用增强（Credit enhancement）大约有三个方式：（1）信用分层（Tranching），将抵押贷款转换成了不同风险等级的证券，满足不同的投资者的需求；（2）超额抵押（Over‑collateralization）：资产池的规模大于对外发行全部证券的本金总和，多出的那一部分资产就是超额抵押，用来吸纳亏损；（3）超额利差（Excess spread）：抵押贷款利率高于MBS的利率，保证利差为正。
CDO（Collateralized Debt Obligation）将以次级贷款为底层资产的MBS再次进行证券化、分层，转换成不同等级的证券。此外，CDS（Credit Default Swap）给抵押贷款加上一层“保险”，进一步提升其流动性。

数据显示，1980年代以后，美国贷款/GDP比例大幅上升，其中居民地产贷款上升最多。1995年，居民抵押贷款与GDP之比不足50%，而2007年该比例超过80%。从2001年到2006年，美国抵押贷款证券化比例大幅上升，特别是Alt-A和Sub-prime这些质量较差的抵押贷款证券化比例上升较快。例如，Alt-A级抵押贷款的证券化比例从19%（2001年）上升到了91%（2006年），Sub-prime级抵押贷款的证券化比例从46%（2001年）上升到了75%（2006年）。
美国抵押贷款持有人从银行转向非银。早期美国住宅证券化主要由Fannie Mae、Freddie Mac、Ginnie Mae等政府支持机构参与，后期越来越多的非政府支持机构开始参与抵押贷款证券化（包括投资银行）。通过证券化方式，政府支持机构（如房地美、房利美）、ABS发行人持有占比2006年超过60%。

资产证券化或成为美国AI公司融资的下一步。随着长期租赁和容量采购合同不断累积，数据中心与算力资产的稳定现金流开始具备证券化条件。2024年初，CyrusOne发行了11.75亿美元的数据中心资产支持证券（ABS）[6]；2025年3月，Sabey发行3.25亿美元ABS，抵押品是在美国的7个数据中心[7]；2025年5月，Stack发行3.45亿美元ABS，抵押品是11个美国数据中心的房地产、租赁和相关权益[8]；2025年9月，QTS发行6亿美元ABS，抵押品是Phoenix的数据中心[9]；2026年初，Compass Datacenters发行了8.3亿美元的数据中心ABS，底层资产即为向云厂商租赁算力的长期合约[10]。AI数据中心贷款正被打包成ABS，向养老金、保险资金等机构投资者分销，类似于房地产证券化过程。
美国AI企业长期股权投资近期开始抬升，但总体占比不高。AI企业的对外长期股权投资自2025年以来抬升，到2026Q2在总资产中的占比约为5%。相比于科网企业，AI企业长期股权投资占比不高，显示AI企业的股权金融还处于早期。而且，通过将部分重资产项目以股权投资方式，剥离出超大规模云厂商的资产负债表，也是风险隔离的一种方式。

注：各组为样本公司先分别计算比率后简单平均。AI企业包括微软、Alphabet、亚马逊、Meta、甲骨文

短期风险
前面的分析意味着，在美国金融化的大背景下，加上AI公司既有比科网公司更强的科技属性，又有“类地产”属性，AI公司既可以通过股权融资，也可以通过债权融资。而与历史上的科网革命和房地产相比，美国AI公司当前金融化尚处于早期阶段，其资金来源无需过度担忧。但这不是说，我们就可以忽视短期的流动性波动风险，尤其是油价居高不下、美国加息路径不清晰的情况下。

回顾历史，当年美国科网泡沫与地产泡沫破灭前同时出现三个现象：（1）高杠杆。科网革命时期，美国大量Dotcom公司上市，Shiller PE ratio从17倍（1990年）上涨到44倍（2000年）。次贷危机前，美国家庭部门宏观杠杆率从70%（2000年）上升到98%（2007年）；（2）基本面走弱。2000年左右，美国互联网用户渗透率出现拐点，而2006年开始，美国房贷违约率开始上升；（3）融资条件系统性收紧。美联储从1998年开始加息，联邦基金利率从4.75%（1998年）上升至6.5%（2000年）。次贷危机前，联邦基金利率从1.0%（2003年）上升到5.23%（2006年）。
当前，对于AI公司来说，这三个现象特征都还不显著。目前美国企业部门杠杆率相对还较低，股市估值也不算非常高；美国经济基本还比较强劲，名义增长在5%左右，以Mag 7为代表的大科技公司营收、利润增速还较高；融资条件暂时还未见明显持续的收紧。
但是，短期风险仍需要关注，可能对AI企业融资产生扰动。目前美国融资需求旺盛，而随着通胀上升，资金面边际紧张。近期，实际融资压力（实际利率TIPs）走高，市场对AI产业链高杠杆的持续性产生顾虑。

2026年9月，英格兰央行金融政策委员会指出AI债务上升，以及其不够透明，对风险评估带来困难，而随着金融条件收紧，信贷市场（包括私募信贷）相对比较脆弱[11]。2026年5月，美联储在《金融稳定报告》中指出，AI以及私募信贷是近期需要关注的风险[12]。美联储认为随着资本支出越来越多地依赖债务融资，增加了系统的杠杆效应；私人信贷面临着越来越大的压力，包括投资者的赎回、情绪恶化，以及人工智能带来的信贷质量影响。2026年9月，标普将Oracle的评级下调至BBB-，仅高于垃圾级[13]。自美联储在2026年9月加息后，到9月底，Coreweave一些高收益债的收益率上涨了超过0.5个百分点[14]。2026年7月，Meta新发120亿美元债券，为数据中心进行融资，债券收益率为7.5%，融资成本要比2025年10月发行270亿美元债券时高出0.4个百分点[15]。
图表30：泡沫破灭一般出现在融资条件系统性收紧之后
资料来源：iFinD，中金公司研究部
具体来看，短期需关注两类风险。一是融资条件收紧，削弱私人投资动能。若美联储加息，或银行收紧贷款标准，企业融资成本和资金获取难度可能上升，进而拖累私人投资扩张。二是短期融资压力加剧，放大流动性风险。回购与资产支持商业票据市场利差仍高于常态，提示部分市场主体的短期融资压力尚未消退。若此时货币政策进一步收紧，可能增加债务续借难度，并放大短期资金市场的波动。

items.title: 对冲基金减持科技股，Mag 7持仓却创历史新高！高盛：市场处处创纪录，唯独缺乏信心
items.summary: 标普屡创新高之际，市场内部正在发生截然相反的事情。对冲基金一边抛售科技股，一边将"Mag
items.text:
标普屡创新高之际，市场内部正在发生截然相反的事情。对冲基金一边抛售科技股，一边将"Mag 7"持仓推至历史峰值；信心指标跌至极端低位，而各类资产的仓位数据却在不断刷新纪录。高盛的最新周报揭示，表面平静之下，市场的结构性张力从未如此之大。


上周标普500指数上涨1.2%至7811点，再创历史新高。然而据高盛的数据，对冲基金净杠杆率仅为46.9%，处于过去一年的第2百分位；多空比进一步跌至1.565，位于五年回望的第1百分位。与此同时，科技股遭遇连续净卖出，领跌行业正是此前四周内四度蝉联最受追捧板块的信息技术。


市场结构性分歧还体现在衍生品定价上。高盛衍生品团队指出，VIX上行凸性极度受追捧，而标普500下行保护却"极度廉价"——用其同事的话说，"VIX升至25以上的概率，几乎高于标普500下跌2%的概率"。这一异常信号表明，投资者对尾部风险的定价方向，已从担忧股市下行转向防范波动率本身的跳升。

轮动方向：从芯片到飞机与导弹

资金流向是本周最清晰的叙事线索。高盛prime book数据显示，在过去五周内连续净卖出工业股后，对冲基金本周以年初以来最快速度净买入工业板块（+1.8个标准差），几乎完全由做多驱动，领涨子行业包括航空航天与国防、建筑与工程、航空公司及工业集团。


科技板块内部同样出现明显分化。半导体与科技硬件是被减持最多的子行业，软件则是唯一实现净买入的方向。高盛TMT专家Pete Callahan指出，过去一周软件跑赢半导体约800个基点，高盛软件/半导体对冲组合单周涨幅达11.8%。


此次轮动的导火索有迹可循。上周四，《金融时报》报道OpenAI营收数据令人失望，纳斯达克当日大幅下挫。高盛数据显示，周四正是科技股净卖出最为集中的交易日，兼有多头减仓与空头增加，"指向获利了结与对冲需求同步上升"。

Mag 7持仓创历史新高，信心却跌至谷底

矛盾之处在于：对冲基金大规模减持科技股，但对最大科技股的敞口却从未如此之高。高盛股票部门数据显示，Mag 7仓位占其美股总敞口的比例已从6月的年内低点14%迅速攀升至22%，创prime book历史最高纪录。


摩根士丹利prime brokerage数据从另一侧印证了这一判断：信息技术目前占对冲基金北美净敞口的32%，处于2010年以来的第98百分位。换言之，行业层面的卖出并不意味着低配——没有人真正减少了对这一赛道的暴露。


与此同时，基本面多空基金的表现持续承压。据高盛Prime Services周报估算，10月2日至8日期间，平均基本面多空基金下跌0.70%，而MSCI全球指数上涨0.78%，亏损"几乎完全来自阿尔法端的多空两侧损失"。年初至今，基本面多空策略回报率为11.82%，落后于MSCI的12.42%与标普500的14.45%。系统化策略同期上涨21.40%，量化持续跑赢人工判断。

财报季开幕：高标准，低奖励

财报季将于本周正式开启，大型银行率先登场。


高盛股票部门直接点明挑战所在：共识预期标普500每股盈利同比增长27%，为2021年以来最高，而中位数个股的预期增速仅为9%（上季度为14%）。这一落差背后，是美光和英伟达两家公司单独承担本季度约三分之一的盈利增长。


更值得关注的是"超预期不奖励"现象。


高盛数据显示，上季度盈利超预期的个股相对标普500的超额表现仅为35个基点，远低于历史均值95个基点。美光录得1003%的每股盈利增速，全面超预期，市场反应却相当克制。高盛就此发问：这一"高标准困境"是否已蔓延至整个AI板块？


银行股面临的处境尤为特殊。高盛衍生品团队指出，金融板块从高点回调幅度约为期权隐含单日波动的五倍，但市场对其财报日的定价却极为温和。摩根士丹利下跌20%，期权定价隐含涨跌幅仅为3.7%；美国银行下跌19%，对应隐含波动为3.4%。


高盛金融行业专家Christian DeGrasse指出，市场对银行的情绪"明显转向谨慎"，争议焦点在于三季度活动放缓究竟是"短暂停顿"还是"持续下行的信号"。


摩根士丹利的Nick Savone走得更远：美国银行股相对标普500的超卖程度已达1993年以来最高，14日RSI约为27，BKX远期市盈率已跌破十年中位数。

OpenAI事件的连锁反应：债市意外受益

上周四，OpenAI营收数据引发的市场波动不仅波及股市，也意外推动了长债价格反弹。高盛期货团队指出，长债"可能终于在本周触底"，而触发反弹的正是OpenAI相关头条。


逻辑在于：一旦AI资本开支扩张预期出现松动，此前被AI融资需求持续挤压的美债久期买盘便有望回流。此前，资产管理公司在长债上的空头头寸自9月中旬以来急剧上升，若周四的走势触发这批空头回补，则债市在下周初或将获得进一步支撑——不过这一反弹能否持续，仍取决于周二的CPI数据。


黄金方面，本周上涨1.3%，"维持在每盎司4100美元以上"。高盛期货团队指出，系统化策略仓位已降至一年回望的第0百分位，CFTC管理资金净多头也回归正常水平，认为"增加黄金多头头寸的吸引力正在上升"。

电力：高盛眼中"最被低估的AI瓶颈"

高盛主题篮子团队将旗下"Power Up America"篮子（代码GSENEPOW）称为"最被低估的AI瓶颈"，并将这一判断建立在三个维度之上：仓位处于近两年低位、估值已回归正常、基本面依然稳健。该篮子本周上涨4.9%，独立发电商子板块涨幅达12.7%。


团队认为，市场对中期选举及电力政策政治化的担忧"正在消退"，预计未来将通过电网建设与"表后用电"方案刺激美国电力供给。高盛预测，到2030年，"表后用电"将满足全美25%数据中心的用电需求。近期关键催化剂包括：FERC就PJM大负荷框架于10月12日周一作出裁决，以及PJM相关文件与ERCOT数据中心并网审计结果。

items.title: Mourners killed by Kenya police at ex-PM's national farewell not part of violence, BBC finds
items.summary: Three mourners killed when Kenyan police opened fire at a national farewell for former Prime Minister Raila Odinga were not involved in a clash that sparked
items.text:
Three mourners killed when Kenyan police opened fire at a national farewell for former Prime Minister Raila Odinga were not involved in a clash that sparked gunfire, a BBC Africa Eye investigation has found.

During an event held last October for people to pay their respects to Odinga, three people were shot dead after mourners attempted to gain access to the VIP section of Nairobi's Kasarani Stadium by force.

BBC analysis from inside the stadium shows the victims were each between at least 60m (197 ft) and 160m from the scuffles.

Kenya's Interior Minister Kipchumba Murkomen told the BBC that the police action had been "restrained" after the crowd starting throwing stones.

In footage analysed by the BBC, it is clear that objects, including plastic chairs, are thrown, but we have no evidence that they included stones.

The BBC went through more than 1,500 images and videos to establish the location of those killed in the stadium on 16 October 2025, and also spoke to some of their relatives.

Forensic analysis by the BBC suggests an elite police unit responsible for protecting the president may have fired the fatal shots.

Kenya's longest serving opposition leader and former prime minister died the previous day while receiving medical treatment in India. He was one of the country's most influential political figures.

A year on, Kenya's police watchdog, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA), is still investigating the deaths and police response and no-one has been held to account.

The interior minister defended the police by saying they had been under "so much pressure" after working for many hours non-stop and had been deployed to a new venue at the last minute.

"The investigations are being done by an independent police oversight authority, we believe that their findings will help us take appropriate legal action," Murkomen said.

Responding to questions about the conduct of police he said: "I don't think… somebody [was] sitting there and saying: 'Shoot now'. It is the judgment of the police officer at the spur of the moment."

Yvonne Akinyi, who husband was among those killed told the BBC: "The people who we look at to protect us, these are the people that cause us this pain. These are the people that make us to become young widows in this country, young orphans in this county," she said.

Odinga's death at 80 prompted an outpouring of grief across Kenya. Thousands gathered at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport as his body was flown home.

The body had originally been due to lie in state at parliament, but the scale of the crowds and fears of a security breach forced a last-minute change of venue to Kasarani Stadium. Officials say they had little time to secure the 48,000-capacity venue, and thousands spilled onto the pitch and into the stands unchecked.

After several hours of waiting to see the coffin in 30C heat with no public address system for official updates, a small section of the crowd began throwing objects, including plastic chairs, at officers guarding the VIP pavilion. Police fired live rounds as mourners pushed toward the pavilion. Footage from elsewhere in the stadium shows the crowd remained largely peaceful.

In total, three people were killed.

One of them was Evans Kiche, a 40 year-old-chef and father to seven children. BBC analysis shows he was around 60m from the confrontation when he was killed by a gunshot wound to the head.

The two other mourners killed, Vincent Ogutu and Jidah Burka, were at least 160m away, in the opposite stands, far removed from the pavilion.

Autopsy reports confirm that Ogutu died from a gunshot wound to the chest and 42 year-old Burka was fatally shot in the head.

Piecing together a timeline of events, BBC Africa Eye identified at least eight police officers operating together, wearing tactical clothing and military camouflage. These officers carry assault rifles, with no visible insignia and faces covered.

Their uniforms and movements are consistent with a layer of security assigned to President William Ruto and other VIPs before and after the shooting. At least three officers of this unit appear to fire their weapons.

The BBC identified three of them as part of an elite police unit responsible for presidential protection.

The BBC cannot establish which bullets killed each victim, and cannot rule out other officers firing inside the stadium.

Kenya's National Police Service told the BBC: "There are huge lessons picked from the day's events," which had "formed a fundamental learning curve for a better, more professional application in the future." The IPOA did not respond to a request for comment.

Ogutu, a 36-year-old father of three, hadn't planned to go to Kasarani, his wife told the BBC. He was in central Nairobi on the morning of 16 October with friends when they saw the crowds heading to the stadium and decided to join.

Within hours, he was dead.

His widow Yvonne Akinyi described how the killing upended their family, saying their children were now orphans.

As she prepares to mark a year since her husband's death, Akinyi is no closer to understanding why he died while paying his respects at an event organised by the government.

"I will just try to be that strong woman. Very strong. But deep inside there is a hole," she said.

"It is very painful because sometimes you just sit down and ask yourself. At Kasarani there were so many people, so many of them. Why him."

items.title: One killed, 11 injured in second Houthi strike on Riyadh airport in two days

A Saudi military
items.text:
One person has been killed and 11 injured in a second strike on the international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, officials have said.

A Saudi military spokesman said a projectile had hit King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, causing a fire in a passenger hall. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said in a statement on X that one person, a Pakistani resident, had been killed in the attack.

It comes a day after a strike on the same airport killed 13 people and injured 308 others. There have been a series of other attacks earlier in the week.

The Houthis in Yemen said they were behind them and warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi Arabian airports and airspace.

The group said they had targeted the airport with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones in the past 24 hours.

They also attacked oil facilities and Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, their military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree said.

He vowed to continue the "escalating operations deep inside Saudi Arabia", warning that all Saudi airports were potential targets apart from those in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

The Houthis have said they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war, as well as an air strike on the airport in Sanaa.

On Sunday Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition, said air defences had intercepted a missile near the airport in Riyadh, while authorities were dealing with the fire caused by an "unknown projectile" that hit Passenger Hall No 4.

US President Donald Trump has said the US would "make a decision" and "move very quickly" on whether to strike the Houthis, while UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting suggested the UK could "potentially" provide more support for Saudi Arabia.

Saturday's strike was the deadliest single attack on a Gulf Arab country since the war between Israel, the US and Iran began in February. The Saudi-led coalition vowed to respond, calling it a "war crime".

Four Saudi nationals, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt were among the dead, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.

The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said on Sunday that an Indian man had succumbed to the injuries he sustained in the attack.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks and confirmed that a US citizen was killed in the strikes. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said he was "appalled".

The UK Foreign Office is advising against all travel to parts of Saudi Arabia, including areas within 10km (6.2 miles) of the border with Yemen, while other western embassies have warned their nationals about travel in the region.

Houthi-run Al Masirah TV said "the Saudi enemy" had launched an air strike on Sanaa International Airport in Yemen's capital. A residential home in the city was also struck, killing a child and injuring six people, the media outlet reported.

Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the attacks and the BBC has been unable to verify this report.

Abdullah Al-Alimi Bawazir, vice-president of Yemen's internationally recognised government, called for "decisive actions" from regional and international partners.

Riyadh's airport was struck on Thursday, an attack that killed three Saudi nationals. The Houthis claimed responsibility and said they had used cruise missiles to target the airport.

There were two other deadly attacks on Saudi airports in Abha and Riyadh in the two days prior to that.

The latest uptick in violence comes after a temporary ceasefire between the Houthis and Saudi-led forces, brokered in 2022, collapsed in July.

The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive, prompting Saudi strikes. Yemeni pro-government forces later said they had secured the regions.

The Houthis currently control around a quarter of Yemeni territory and as much as 80% of the country's population. The Iran-backed armed group hopes to eventually seize complete control.

Saudi Arabia fears this would lead to the establishment of an Iranian satellite state on its southern border.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told his Saudi Arabian counterpart on Sunday that his country was ready to provide assistance to "facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen", referring to the Houthi administration.

items.title: Passkeys are a trap
items.author: laurex
items.summary: Seems like every website wants us to stop using passwords. There is a replacement we are being asked to use instead called passkeys. This should be a tad
items.text:
Seems like every website wants us to stop using passwords. There is a replacement we are being asked to use instead called passkeys. This should be a tad concerning if passwords are familiar to you and you don’t fully understand these nebulous passkeys.

Websites say that passkeys are more secure or more convenient or something similarly beneficial. While it is true that passkeys can be far more secure than passwords, and may indeed be more convenient, that’s not the whole story. Passkeys are not designed to prioritize your interests. Like the Trojan Horse, passkeys are legitimately elegant on the surface, but there is something troubling inside.

What’s important to know is that unlike with any other kind of login credential, you do not have ultimate control over your passkeys. With passwords, you can choose where to write them down; with authenticator apps, you can decide for yourself which ones to use (they’re pretty interchangeable); and with physical security keys you can hand them to your colleague if you really trust them. But with passkeys come a hidden dial that lets the websites you use them on gradually remove your ability to do as you please with them.

I will explain how that is possible further down, but let’s first take a look at who wants you to be using passkeys.

Passkeys are the invention of the FIDO Alliance, which is a consortium of a number of different competing interests – Big Tech, little tech, national governments, intelligence agencies, banks, various public institutions, and even a handful of nonprofits like Mozilla – who are all able to agree that passkeys are a good and righteous cause.

The members of the FIDO Alliance all have their own interests. Big Tech wants to bring little inconveniences into our life so they can sell us more ads. Intelligence agencies want to track everyone in the world. Banks want to be free of indemnity. Little tech wants cheap solutions to reduce liability. Mozilla wants to avoid having to die on any particular hill. I make no particular claim that any of these are bad motivations. But it is notable that no consumer advocacy groups are members of the FIDO Alliance. (This stands in contrast to, for example, the World Wide Web Consortium, the organization that decides the standards used on the web. Alongside the usual corporate members it has not only public interest groups but also universities and Tim Berners-Lee, the British computer scientist who invented the World Wide Web in 1989. Honestly, if Gandalf himself were to join the W3C he would not be out of place.) Regarding the FIDO Alliance, nobody is there to make a strong case for the user’s own interests.

The reason presented to the public for why everyone needs to use passkeys now is that passwords are insecure. On this point I agree. Consider that the servers behind the billion-dollar American IT company SolarWinds were famously found to be using solarwinds123. Hawaii’s Emergency Management Agency (the same one that sent out that false missile alert) accidentally revealed a password due to a sticky note on someone’s desk in the background of a photograph. If your security relies on a password, you will always be anxious that somebody, somewhere, has somehow figured out what it is and already has access to your bank account.

On the other hand: what passwords have going for them is that they’re very intuitive, everyone knows how they work, people have been using them since time immemorial, and you can choose where you store them and who you share them with. Keep this in mind.

(Also keep this in mind: Netflix does not want you to share your passwords.)

But there already exist superior security mechanisms to passwords, to which the FIDO Alliance seems to be giving the cold shoulder: first there was Two-Factor Authentication (in particular: receiving a text message or email with a one-time code), and later came the more robust system of Time-Based One-Time Passwords (TOTP) – in common parlance, “authenticator apps.”

What’s neat about TOTP is that it doesn’t rely on text messages or email or even the internet at all. Your authenticator software simply generates a random-looking number every 30 seconds based on the current time (and a random starting number called a “seed” or a “key” that is unique to you), and this is all that a website needs to verify you’re you. The term authenticator app is misleading, not in the least because websites tend to heavily imply you need to download a specific app, such as Google Authenticator. In reality, there is an open standard for TOTP (called RFC 6238); that is to say, the formula used to generate these random-looking numbers is public knowledge, so you don’t need to use any one specific piece of software. In almost all cases you don’t need to use Google Authenticator just because the website suggests it. You don’t even need to use a smartphone; you can use your laptop or even a Game Boy from the 90s for this purpose. You can use any software and hardware you like, so long as it can tell time decently and can handle a few lines of code. You can even write the software yourself in Python if you want, or if you feel like burning a moticum of jet fuel you can get an LLM to write it for you.

Both kinds exist.

Although it’s how physical objects have always worked, we don’t often encounter situations in the digital world where sending something to your friend causes it to disappear from your own device.

You might want your passkey to be non-transferable in order to be completely sure that physical possession of one specific device is absolutely required to access your account. On the other hand, you might want your non-copyable passkey to be transferable in order for it to be able to move with you when you replace your smartphone for next year’s model. (Or maybe you just want to be able to play some kind of avant-garde digital relay race among your friends as an artistic statement.)

Both kinds exist.

Even if you’re not digitally savvy, you probably know what files and folders are, at least if you have a desktop computer. Admittedly, smartphones are designed to muddy the waters regarding where exactly that file you downloaded is and if folders are even a copacetic concept. (Yes, smartphones do use files and folders. They just don’t typically come with a file browser like your desktop does.)

So all these passkeys we’ve talked about so far are just files right? Well… not really. That is, they can be. Or they might not be. As with all these other qualities a passkey can optionally have, passkeys can optionally not be files at all. Indeed, since files are copyable and transferable and all sorts of other intuitive things, if passkeys had to be files, it would not be clear how anyone could make a non-copyable passkey.

Enter hardware-backed passkeys. These make use of a secure chip that comes with all modern devices which can store data that cannot be exfiltrated (meaning the data cannot leave the safety of the secure chip). There are different kinds of chips with different names: your laptop has a Trusted Platform Module and an iPhone has a “Secure Enclave” and so on. You will not find this area of your device in your file browser anywhere. It is a separate component entirely. Because of their cryptographic use case (and perhaps their mystique), people have taken to calling these chips “cryptoprocessors.”

The consensus seems to be that cryptoprocessors are indeed very secure. You might wonder if someone with the know-how couldn’t just surgically open the chip with the right tools and extract the data off that way. That’s theoretically possible; however, such chips employ all kinds of chemical and electronic tamper-detection measures and will self-destruct if you try to do this. So unless you have the resources of a nation-state at your disposal, you can basically take as a given that (hypothetical manufacturer backdoors notwithstanding) nobody can remove the secret data from your cryptoprocessor; not Netflix, not your operating system, not even you.

You might prefer to use a software-backed key because you understand how files work and you already have a solution that works for you for storing your private data. You might want to use a hardware-backed key to get the extra security afforded by a nigh-impenetrable cryptoprocessor.

Both kinds exist.

Some passkeys require somebody to press a button or click a prompt to confirm authentication. Others can be used without anyone in the loop at all.

You might want the former kind because you yourself are a human. You might want the latter kind in case you want to authorize a piece of software to act on your behalf.

Both kinds exist.

Okay so maybe a user was present, but how do we know the right user was present? Passkeys can optionally require biometrics (e.g. fingerprint sensors or retina scanners) or the use of PINs or passwords of their own in order to be extra sure that only one specific intended human being can use them.

You might want a user-verified passkey in order to be safe even in the situation a thief pilfers your device. You might want a non-user-verified passkey because you expect to lend your tablet to another family member so they can read your ebooks on Amazon and listen to music on your Spotify account and watch your movies on Disney+.

This is where things take a left turn.

I’ve presented all these properties so far as being up to you to decide. That may indeed be how it is on most websites – for now, at least. After all, what cause does Twitter have to tell me exactly which security measures out of the smorgasbord available I should opt into for my passkeys? But you should know that the FIDO Alliance has defined this standard such that your passkey software is required to tell the service you’re accessing which of these features are enabled. They’re called authenticator data flags in the WebAuthn standard.

This means Twitter (formally X) can say to you, “sorry, we only accept the User-Present User-Verified Non-Copyable Hardware-Backed varieties of passkey here. But hey! You can still choose between Transferable and Non-Transferable passkeys!” Actually, I’m being optimistic – I suspect they are unlikely to phrase it in such clear terms. They will likely just say “unfortunately your passkey isn’t secure enough; download our app.”

But it’s an open standard, isn’t it? And maybe you have a friend experienced in writing Python code. Can’t you just make your own passkey software which just does the nice file-based kind of passkeys with none of those extra security features, and then have it tell the website anyway that it’s a User-Present User-Verified Non-Copyable Hardware-Backed passkey? Can’t you just lie?

Oh yes absolutely you can. Your passkey software can lie about whatever passkey features you like. Unless we’re talking about an Attested User-Present User-Verified Non-Copyable Hardware-Backed passkey. In which case, no. That can’t be faked.

Attested passkeys are the last but most important type of passkeys you need to know about. These types of keys use what’s known as remote attestation to cryptographically verify – using the aforementioned tamper-proof cryptoprocessor that lives in all your modern devices – that you are using one of the several approved passkey managers, and not using a custom one that you vibecoded yourself and which can lie.

This is the feature that means you no longer get to make the calls about your passkeys. Fortunately, attested passkeys are not yet required on most websites. But the FIDO Alliance standard makes attestation a part of the passkey ecosystem, whether you want it or not. And even if the website doesn’t require attestation now, simply by using passkeys you indicate to the website that your setup supports the FIDO Alliance’s passkey standard and that you as a user are capable of using passkeys. This means that once Twitter (formally X) is satisfied that the overwhelming majority of its users would be unaffected, they can flip the switch – perhaps not all at once, perhaps just for ten thousand users at a time so as not to cause a fuss – and start rejecting non-attested passkeys.

Critically, remote attestation requires the co-operation of your cryptoprocessor, your passkey manager software, your device’s operating system, and your device’s firmware to all pass the remote attestation check. After all, your phone’s operating system has total access to all the 0s and 1s in every app that’s ever run, so it’s not enough for Twitter (formally X) to trust your passkey manager if it can’t even trust your phone’s underlying operating system. I’d like to be clear that there are legitimate uses of remote attestation. By using a website that requires attested passkeys you can be sure you stay safe from accidentally installing a scammer’s fake passkey application that steals your data – the website will reject such a passkey. Though admittedly that guarantee is less reassuring once you realize that even if the key stays firmly on your device a hacker could still use it if they have control of your phone otherwise. Or a phone with a refurbished operating system. (Or if you’re nefarious you might want to be able to lie to Netflix and tell them that of course you and your three friends are absolutely all the same person using the same device.)

There is ample reason for you to be hesitant before you set up a passkey. If you’ve used only websites that require one certain kind of passkey then you might not notice when a website has you set up a different kind of passkey. Don’t forget that unlike passwords and SMS codes and TOTP, passkeys are designed to function in the background without you ever seeing the details. They’ll offer you at most a “confirm” prompt. (That’s the convenience aspect.) My expectation is that the industry will start off with very few constraints on your passkeys, and gradually add more and more, not all at the same time, but staggered on different sites, and then in a few years people will forget that they were ever offered a choice in which security measures they want to enable on their passkeys (if they even knew there were different kinds of passkeys at all).

So far, almost nobody has even heard of remote attestation. The vast majority of people use one of the four major operating systems (Windows, Android, macOS, and iOS) and not alternative operating systems like Linux, LineageOS, postmarketOS, or GrapheneOS. The overwhelming majority of people don’t replace the operating system on their phone when it stops receiving updates; instead they just buy a new phone. So almost nobody will ever encounter a situation where their device fails a remote attestation check.

Are attested passkeys so bad, though? After all, we really aren’t meant be sharing Netflix accounts to begin with.

Take another look at the list of members in the FIDO Alliance, and put on your tinfoil hat. Why do intelligence agencies care if I am sharing my Netflix account? Heck, why does Microsoft care if I am sharing my Netflix account?

For intelligence agencies, and for corporations like Microsoft, Google, Apple, Facebook, Amazon – giving you convenience and security is likely not their primary goal. I think they have an entirely ulterior motive. They can use passkeys to prevent you from running unapproved software.

Remote attestation can allow them to verify that your device is not capable of, say, sending and receiving encrypted messages, or running a competitor’s app, or using social media without verifying your ID. They don’t want you to be able to turn off the mandatory built-in AI image scanner on your phone that scans everything your phone sees for nudity. (Yes, I’m serious.)

But I rather like deciding for myself what software I approve of and what software I don’t. Something I value about my web browser is that I can install extensions to modify aspects of websites that bother me. I can say no to auto-playing videos on news websites; I can decide which advertisements are too intrusive for me to let through; I can filter out irrelevant search results and disable AI summaries; I can block the “recommended video” feature on YouTube which always seems to promote outrage and division (or as Big Tech calls it, “engagement”). And if a website ends up monopolizing my time anyway, I have an extension that locks them down after a certain duration. These extensions give me control over how the internet affects me, even if Big Tech would much rather make those decisions for me. But Google owns Google Chrome, which is the world’s most popular web browser, and they can remove support for these useful extensions (as they did earlier this year with uBlock Origin); and with remote attestation they can prevent me from using any other browser that doesn’t follow suit.

Remember those authenticator data flags I mentioned? There used to be only 4 of them. Earlier revisions of the FIDO Alliance’s security standard (called “WebAuthn Level 1” and “WebAuthn Level 2”) had fewer catalog options to choose from. I’m sweeping some details under the rug here for brevity, but since you are given four distinct binary choices, you could call that 16 different kinds of passkey. In 2022 the FIDO Alliance added some more (“WebAuthn Level 3”), so that websites could know whether or not your credentials are copyable, or if backups of your credentials might exist somewhere. There are still two flags left “reserved for future use.” What might our passkeys require of us in the future?

I’m not one to argue about slippery slopes, so I won’t claim that the campaigns to protect children online today will tomorrow turn into laws designed to make it easy to identify political dissidents. But I will say that the widespread adoption of the passkey technology being advertised to you as convenient and secure is capable of permitting such laws to be easily enforced.

So if you care about your privacy and the privacy of others, if you believe people should be free to choose what software runs on their devices, that people should be allowed to learn how to write their own software and run it on their own devices, and that friends should be able to privately talk politics online without government interference, then I would ask you to reject these dozens of different security mechanisms which are all confusingly branded as the same “passkeys.” Wait for Big Tech to propose something just as convenient and secure but more clearly defined and with fewer strings attached. In the meantime if you want security, your Game Boy can provide you with TOTP.

But it’s an open standard, isn’t it? And maybe you have a friend experienced in writing Python code. Can’t you just make your own passkey software which just does the nice file-based kind of passkeys with none of those extra security features, and then have it tell the website anyway that it’s a User-Present User-Verified Non-Copyable Hardware-Backed passkey? Can’t you just lie?

Oh yes absolutely you can. Your passkey software can lie about whatever passkey features you like. Unless we’re talking about an Attested User-Present User-Verified Non-Copyable Hardware-Backed passkey. In which case, no. That can’t be faked.

Attested passkeys are the last but most important type of passkeys you need to know about. These types of keys use what’s known as remote attestation to cryptographically verify – using the aforementioned tamper-proof cryptoprocessor that lives in all your modern devices – that you are using one of the several approved passkey managers, and not using a custom one that you vibecoded yourself and which can lie.

This is the feature that means you no longer get to make the calls about your passkeys. Fortunately, attested passkeys are not yet required on most websites. But the FIDO Alliance standard makes attestation a part of the passkey ecosystem, whether you want it or not. And even if the website doesn’t require attestation now, simply by using passkeys you indicate to the website that your setup supports the FIDO Alliance’s passkey standard and that you as a user are capable of using passkeys. This means that once Twitter (formally X) is satisfied that the overwhelming majority of its users would be unaffected, they can flip the switch – perhaps not all at once, perhaps just for ten thousand users at a time so as not to cause a fuss – and start rejecting non-attested passkeys.

Critically, remote attestation requires the co-operation of your cryptoprocessor, your passkey manager software, your device’s operating system, and your device’s firmware to all pass the remote attestation check. After all, your phone’s operating system has total access to all the 0s and 1s in every app that’s ever run, so it’s not enough for Twitter (formally X) to trust your passkey manager if it can’t even trust your phone’s underlying operating system. If any single one of those things were to fail – say, because your phone stopped receiving security updates so you installed a custom operating system like LineageOS to keep yourself safe without having to buy a new device – then Twitter (formally X) will be able to notice and prevent you from logging in.

I’d like to be clear that there are legitimate uses of remote attestation. By using a website that requires attested passkeys you can be sure you stay safe from accidentally installing a scammer’s fake passkey application that steals your data – the website will reject such a passkey. You might want an attested Passkey even if the website doesn’t require it, since you can use attestation to verify that your software has not been tampered with by a hacker while you weren’t looking. (Of course, attestation may be overkill for this; even if your device were hacked, the hardware-backing feature described above makes it impossible for the passkey to be exfiltrated from your device. Though admittedly that guarantee is less reassuring once you realize that even if the key stays firmly on your device a hacker could still use it if they have control of your phone otherwise. At the very least you can always power off the device to temporarily deny hackers access to your Non-Attested Hardware-Backed Non-Copyable Non-Transferable passkeys.)
